name: NOCO Genius Boost+ GB40 Jump Starter
description: The NOCO Genius Boost+ GB40 is a portable lithium-ion jump starter rated for 12V vehicles with up to 1000A peak power, designed to start dead batteries safely without relying on a second car. It features heavy-duty clamps, spark-proof and reverse-polarity protection with error indicators, a multi-function LED flashlight, and USB ports for charging phones or recharging the unit. A front battery-level LED display helps confirm readiness before roadside use. Compact enough for a trunk or glove-adjacent storage, it targets everyday gasoline cars and similar 12V systems as an emergency power pack rather than a long-term battery charger.

reviews.content: Dead battery in a parking garage — GB40 fired the car on the first try. Clamps feel solid. Flashlight helped me see the terminals. Keep this in the trunk permanently.
Charged fully before a road trip and it just works. USB-out topped up my phone too. Slightly bulky but worth the peace of mind.
Instructions could be clearer for reverse-polarity warnings. Once I figured the lights out, jump was instant. Build quality is rugged.
Failed to start my older diesel on a cold morning. Might be underpowered for that engine. Fine for my wife's sedan though.
NOCO clamps are thick and bite well. No sketchy sparking. Case is tough. Best safety-oriented jumper pack I've owned.
Unit arrived with 60% charge; wish it shipped fuller. After a top-up it's been reliable for two roadside saves already.
Buttons are glove-friendly. Battery LEDs are easy to read. Only complaint is the cable length is a bit short for some engine bays.
Overpriced versus generic Amazon packs, but the safety features sold me. Didn't regret it when the night jump worked flawlessly.
Spark-proof claims held up when I briefly mismatched orientation — alarm screamed, no damage. That alone justifies the brand.
Heavy for what it is. Lives in the garage more than the car now. When used, it starts mid-size SUVs without drama.
USB input charging is slow overnight. Plan ahead before winter. Jump performance itself is excellent.
Used it on a neighbor's Civic — cranked immediately. Neighborhood hero status achieved. Compact enough for the spare-tire well.
Plastic housing scratched in the trunk. Wish it included a better storage bag. Internals seem fine; cosmetics suffer.
Cold weather start assist worked at 5°F. Absolute confidence booster living in the Midwest.
Manual is tiny and hard to read. Watch a quick video instead. Hardware is straightforward once you know the light codes.
Also doubles as an emergency phone charger on camping trips. Dual-purpose value is real.
Trigger button felt sticky out of box; loosened after a few uses. Jump current is strong. QC is mixed.
Compared with cables-only, this is safer for beginners. Parents bought one after my demo. Highly recommend for new drivers.
Won't replace a full shop charger for maintainence, but for dead-battery emergencies it's perfect.
LED flashlight modes are genuinely useful for tire changes. Underrated feature.
Tried on a truck V8 — struggled then succeeded on second attempt. Borderline for larger engines. Check amps vs your vehicle.
No weird chemical smells, clamps store neatly. Feels like a serious tool not a toy.
App? None needed — thankfully. Physical UI is enough. Less to break.
Left it unused 4 months; still had charge to jump. Self-discharge seems decent if you top up seasonally.
Returned first unit for a dead cell; replacement works. Support was okay, shipping slow.
Polarity protection and error lights make this less scary than old-school cables. Taught my teen with it.
Pricey, but one tow avoided pays for it. Already paid for itself once.
Clamp springs are stiff — good grip, hard on small hands. Performance otherwise great.
Doesn't like being stored in extreme heat; dashboard is a bad idea. Trunk floor is fine. Read the temps.
Connections feel premium vs cheap boosters that melted tips. NOCO branding seems earned here.
One-star reviews scared me; my experience has been flawless for a Corolla. Maybe vehicle dependent.
Port covers keep dirt out. Nice detail. Overall pack is travel-ready.
Could use a clearer 'ready to jump' indicator. Mistimed my first attempt. Second try perfect.
Boat battery assist worked at the dock. Surprised me. Versatile 12V helper.
Fan noise while charging the pack is noticeable on a nightstand. Charge in garage.
Build feels like it survives being tossed under seats. Already scuffed, still works.
Not for hybrids with weird 12V systems without checking the manual. On a normal ICE car: excellent.
Gifted to my dad — he texted a photo after saving a stranger in a lot. Endorsement enough.
Peak amp marketing is confusing versus real cranking. Still started my car from dead flat.
MicroUSB/USB-C charging cable quality is meh. Pack is the star; cable is whatever.
Winter kit essential alongside blanket and water. This is the item I'm gladdest I packed.
Sometimes needs a few seconds after connecting before it arms. Patience. Then strong start.
Cheaper units I've tried failed in the cold. This one didn't. Paying more made sense.
Clamps won't reach on some Euro engine layouts without repositioning the pack. Annoying but workable.
No leaky acid like old jump packs. Lithium convenience is the point. Happy convert.
Status LEDs washed out in bright sun. Shade with your hand. Minor UX nit.
Two years in with occasional use — still jumps. Longevity seems good if you recharge periodically.
Feels safer than asking strangers for a jump. Independence matters late at night.
Not a miracle for badly sulfated batteries that won't hold charge. Diagnosed that after two jumps. Tool is fine; battery was toast.
Bottom line: reliable, safe, trunk-worthy. I'd buy the GB40 again for any gas daily driver.
